`seed`: the machine boots with berth's cloud seed and sets itself up.

What it can do besides `create`, `status` and `destroy`: `start`,
`stop`, `list`, `log`.

PublishFrame.description: What a client sends over the channel stream to publish.

registries.description:
By name: `type` (nexus, npm, raw or docker), `url`, `username` and, for

What a roll-out does: apply the hosts that are behind one after another,
stopping at the first that fails.

all.description: Also the hosts that are current.

force.description: Reboot although sessions run, which ends them.

hosts.description: These hosts, in this order; all saved hosts by name when empty.

warnings.description:
What did not go well without being a failure, such as an update step
that ended badly. One stops the roll-out after this host.

ok.description: Every host is done or current.

names.description: A registry's password or token is `registry/NAME`.

Seed.description: What a new machine is started with to become the host.

user_data.description: cloud-init user data, for the provider's field of that name.

lost.description: It ended with berthd or the host, not by itself.

task.description: The task it was started for, if any.

value.description: Empty when it is not set, and for a token.

SetupClaim.description: The server's token, collected with a setup key.

token.description: The token of berth serve, as in its serve.token.

SetupKey.description: What a setup key says of the server it is for.

expires.description: When the key stops working, in RFC 3339.

input.description: Text for standard input; a process then sees the end of its input.

timeout.description: Seconds after which the command is ended.

Started.description:
The answer to a start with `wait=`: the session and, when it has ended in
time, what it wrote.

cpu.description: Percent busy over 200 ms, all cores together.

extends.description: Tasks it is a step of; it then has no row of its own.

input.description: What the workstation sends on standard input: `secrets`.

oneOf.description:
What the host's configuration was last applied from, when berth
recorded it. An older berthd does not say.

info.description: One API over all hosts, with the inbox and a key-value store. Everything under /v1/hosts/{name}/ that is not named here is that host's own API, passed through unchanged; only the `secrets` task is refused, which `hosts.secrets` stands in for. Over TCP every request carries the server's token or an OAuth 2.0 access token as a bearer, and needs the role its operation names. The routes of the setup key take that key as the bearer instead.
